text:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout to canary-2 reported a sustained error-rate spike on /v1/generate, 5m error_rate=3.2% (> threshold 1.5%). auto-fallback attempted but partial traffic still on canary

alex: saw it, thanks. Can we pin traffic to v2.5.1 for all regions while we investigate? :eyes:

priya: I'm on-call. Repro steps? anything in logs indicating model OOM or tokenization failures?

samuel: quick logs show a lot of 502s from runtime, stack traces referencing kvcache flush in the new kernel path. snippet: ```ERROR runtime/kernel.go: kvcache flush failed: context deadline exceeded```

jamie: customer-impacting? Any SLA alerts firing? Sales asking if we should notify customers preemptively.

oncall-bot: Alert: Latency SLA breaches detected in us-west-2 (p95 580ms, threshold 500ms). Incident severity: P3.

alex: Decision checklist: 1) is rollback automated safe? 2) pin vs full rollback? 3) comms cadence. My proposal: manual rollback of canary-2 -> v2.5.1, pin deploy group for 30m, run smoke, then unpin if green.

priya: agree. Automated rollback didn't fully remove traffic because of a partial split config. I'll execute manual pin now.

priya: /rollout pin canary-2 v2.5.1 --reason "error spike kvcache kernel regression" --until "+30m"

deploy-bot: Rollout change accepted. Traffic for canary-2 pinned to v2.5.1. Previous canary variant demoted.

samuel: pin applied, starting smoke tests (simple generate + prefix cache warm). Will post results in 5m.

jamie: I'll draft a short customer note: "We observed elevated error rates affecting a small fraction of traffic in one region; we pinned to a safe revision and are running verification. No customer action required." Anyone object?

alex: good. Also add internal note for SRE runbook: what failed (kvcache flush timeout) and link to PR id #4321 for the kernel change. We may need to revert the kernel change or adjust timeouts.

samuel: smoke results: 10/10 success, p95 now 210ms. No 502s in the last 2m.

priya: leaving pin in place for full 30m to ensure stability. If green at +30m, we can schedule a canary re-run with debug logging on the kernel path.

alex: comms: jamie please post a brief update to #status and to the active customer channel with the note. ops doc: add rollback commands and note that automated fallback may not fully revert split traffic — manual pin required when split configs are in play.

jamie: posted to #status and customer channel. Also updated the internal release notes: "Canary v2.6.0 pinned due to runtime kvcache flush timeouts; rolled back to v2.5.1 in canary-2. Investigation assigned to @samuel. Follow-up: rollback vs pin decision doc link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollback-decision"

samuel: created a follow-up issue: "investigate kvcache flush timeouts in improved kernel path" and linked logs + repro.

priya: closing loop: if anything spikes again, escalate to P2 and consider full cluster revert. For now keeping as P3 and monitoring. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks team. We'll do a postmortem in the next 48h if root cause requires code revert. For now, keep communications tight and update this thread with any changes.
